title: Understanding `with`
body: ### Why look at `with` at all Vue 2's compiler turns a template into an AST, then a render function, then VNodes. The generated render function uses `with`, and that is where the performance problem comes from. ### Why Vue 2 used it `with` extends the scope chain, so code inside the block can reach other variables without any ceremony. It made the compiler's job much simpler. ### What it costs 1. `with` turns variable lookup — walking the scope chain — into implicit runtime behaviour. V8 cannot optimise it at compile time. 2. `with` keeps the entire enclosing function scope alive, not just the block itself. The scope chain has to stay in memory in case something looks a name up in it, which leaks. > How the implicit lookup works: check whether the object has the property, and if not, walk up. The walk itself is not slow. The problem is what it prevents: > 1. the engine will not optimise code inside `with` aggressively; > 2. the JIT skips deep optimisation of the block; > 3. inlining, constant folding, and the rest are all disabled. - - ### `catch` compared with `with` `catch` also has its own scope, and it also extends the scope chain to introduce the error parameter `e`. 1. `try`/`catch`: TurboFan can still optimise most of the `try` block; it is only conservative on the exception path. 2. `with`: still an optimisation black hole, and the whole scope pays for it. 3. In practice: `try`/`catch` is necessary and the cost is acceptable. `with` is avoidable — Vue 3 dropped it.
